cells.tense: Right now, you can let a thing end when it's actually done.
cells.verb: ending what has finished so something new has room
cells.place: in the open hand where you set down what you no longer need
cells.ask: Let something come back in to fill the space you cleared — in fair measure, without keeping a ledger of what you gave up to make it. The endings stay honored, and what comes after keeps showing up.
cells.core:
You can let something end when it's done, and you don't need a fight to do it. You feel when a thing has finished, you put it down, and you trust the room it leaves won't stay empty for long. The grief is real and so is the space — you're holding both without rushing either.

That kind of ending clears ground. You're free to let something new walk onto it: give what's fair, take what's fair, and don't count too hard.
cells.sheetLine: You end what's finished and trust what comes next.

cells.tense: You're already bracing for the next ending before this one has had a chance to be anything.
cells.verb: cutting things loose before they've lived
cells.place: in the open hand that opens too soon
cells.ask: Stay with one thing — a person, a plan, a place — long enough to actually feel what it is, and let it feel you back, without deciding yet whether it stays. Endings arrive when they're ready, not when you're scared.
cells.core:
You're clearing the deck before anything on it has had time to grow. Somewhere ahead there's a lighter, freer version of your life, and you keep reaching for it by letting go — but the deck keeps refilling with things that never got to finish, because you left before they could. Setting things down has started to look a lot like leaving.

The way back isn't holding tighter. It's staying in contact. Let one thing get close enough to know you, and find out what it actually is before you call it done.
cells.sheetLine: You're letting go before anything has had the chance to mean something.

cells.tense: You're still standing at a door that's already closed.
cells.verb: holding on to what has already ended
cells.place: in the hand that won't open
cells.ask: Pick one thing you actually want — not should want, want — and take one real step toward it this week. Your hands will loosen to reach for it. What's finished gets to be finished, and you get to trust what's coming.
cells.core:
You're holding something that's already over. You call it loyalty, and some of it is — but the thing you're loyal to has stopped answering, and you're still showing up for it. Your hands are full with it, so nothing new can get picked up.

Don't try to pry them open. Prying never works. Point yourself at something that pulls you forward, something you genuinely want, and start moving toward it. The grip lets go on its own when there's somewhere better for the hand to be.
cells.sheetLine: You've stayed loyal to something that already ended.

cells.tense: Something in your life is already over, and you haven't told yourself.
cells.verb: ending something without knowing it's ending
cells.place: in the hand that has already loosened without you noticing
cells.ask: Make two plain lists — what you're still really doing, and what you've quietly stopped. Don't explain either one; just let them sit side by side. The ending shows itself, and once it's named, you can honor it and trust what comes after.
cells.core:
You're still going through the motions of something — showing up, keeping the shape of it — but the feeling has already gone out of it, and you'd describe this as fine, just tired. The ending is happening. It's just happening without a name, so it looks like weather instead of a choice.

You don't have to decide anything yet. Simply put it in order: what's still alive in your days and what's already gone quiet. Seen plainly, it makes sense, and what makes sense you can hold.
cells.sheetLine: Something is ending and you're calling it tiredness.

flags.detail: "a while ago" — a cell knows no one's past
